description: treat-sim is a small, fully documented discrete event simulation of an urgent care treatment centre, built as the worked example of the STARS framework (Sharing Tools and Artefacts for Reusable Simulations in healthcare). It was written by Tom Monks, Alison Harper and Amy Heather at the University of Exeter with support from the National Institute for Health Research Applied Research Collaboration South West Peninsula and later the Medical Research Council. The SimPy model follows patients from arrival through triage, registration, examination, and trauma or non-trauma treatment, with time-dependent arrivals taken by default from Nelson (2013) and an alternative arrival profile skewed to the end of the day, and reports waiting times and resource use for scenario comparison. It is generic in location: users set arrival profiles, resource counts and activity times. The package installs from PyPI, runs in the browser through Binder, has a Docker image and automated tests, is archived on Zenodo, and is released under the MIT licence free of charge. Caveats: it is a teaching and reproducibility example, not a calibrated model of a real site, and it has no links to ambulances, inpatient beds or other hospital units. Simulation uses: prototyping emergency department and urgent care capacity planning studies, teaching reproducible healthcare simulation, and testing staffing scenarios. Related records: Ciw (model-ciw-queueing-network-simulation) is an alternative queueing library, and the KHP patient flow simulator (model-khp-patient-flow-simulator) models a real hospital.
